note: Hand-authored evidence mapping from Libella's executed units to ASVS 5.0.0 requirements. Strength: direct = the check exercises the property the requirement states; partial = it exercises part of it; indirect = it records a related observation only. A requirement listed here is NOT claimed as verified by a passing run. `controls` restricts a multi-control check to findings that asserted that control id (see controls.py); titles are never consulted.

rows.why: reads the response headers of the application and reports which security headers are absent
reads Set-Cookie on a response and reports session cookies set without Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite
sends a foreign Origin header and reads Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Credentials back

probes .env/.git/backup files, /actuator, /server-status and /debug for reachable source, debug and monitoring surfaces; each finding carries the control id of the path that answered, so a debug page is never evidence about source metadata
supplies an off-site URL in a parameter and follows the Location header
injects a script canary into one parameter and checks whether it is returned unescaped
error-based injection probe on one parameter of one endpoint
UNION data-extraction proof on an operator-declared parameter
two arithmetic template payloads must both evaluate in the response
sends a traversal payload in one parameter and requires target file content in the response
SQL injection payload against the configured login form; a bypass is an injection defect at the authentication handler
uploads a script file type and fetches it back to see whether the server stored and served it
operator-declared internal URL must be fetched by the application and its marker returned
authenticated read of another identity's object by id, compared with the expected denial; also the unauthenticated variant (the same record served with no credential), by id walk or a declared id
the intent role that runs every WebChecks method above

rows.note: agent web role drives the same WebChecks methods

rows.why: records the server header and technology banner of the response
ProjectDiscovery httpx fingerprint: server header, title, technology tags
reads version-bearing response headers as an observation, not a control test
template-dependent: only the exposed-file, debug and misconfiguration families are relevant, and only when those templates ran
wordlist discovery of unreferenced files and admin paths
passive ZAP rules cover header, cookie and disclosure checks only
reads the negotiated protocol, cipher suite and certificate of the endpoint
the infra intent runs tls_audit; nmap adds port/service context but tests no ASVS requirement
agent infra role runs the TLS audit and host scans
OpenAPI-driven object-level, function-level and mass-assignment probes across the declared roles; credential fields returned in collection responses

rows.note: agent api role drives the same api_audit probes

rows.why: logs every declared identity in and compares each identity's access to each endpoint (GET) with the expected-authorization rule; a blocked sweep is recorded inconclusive, never as a pass
agent authz role attempts authentication and object/function authorization bypasses
introspection, per-role object/function authorization queries and injection probes
static review of the supplied source: semgrep rules, repository secrets, dependency and image CVEs
image component CVEs, mapped to the component-remediation requirement only

unmapped.crawl: endpoint and route discovery feeds other checks but tests no ASVS requirement
unmapped.nmap: port and service enumeration is context for the TLS requirement, which tls_audit tests
unmapped.subfinder: subdomain enumeration discovers assets, it does not verify a control
unmapped.cloud_audit: cloud account posture sits outside the application requirements in ASVS
unmapped.verify: replays a candidate's proof; tests nothing new
unmapped.correlator: reads recorded state, no target traffic
unmapped.risk: scores recorded findings, no target traffic
unmapped.run_baseline: runs the web_checks surface, whose methods are mapped individually
unmapped.http_write: permission marker for agent write requests, not a test

manual.V1: source-level encoding and sanitization review of every sink
manual.V2: input validation and business-logic review against the intended workflow
manual.V3: browser-rendered frontend review, DOM inspection and client-side control testing
manual.V4: per-endpoint API protocol review including GraphQL cost controls and WebSocket handshakes
manual.V5: file handling review with upload/download workflows and storage configuration
manual.V6: authentication workflow review across every pathway, including MFA and recovery
manual.V7: session lifecycle review with re-authentication, timeout and termination tests
manual.V8: authorization review across every role and object, including field-level rules
manual.V9: self-contained token validation review against issuer and audience configuration
manual.V10: OAuth/OIDC authorization-server and client configuration review
manual.V11: cryptographic inventory and implementation review of the application stack
manual.V12: certificate, trust-store and internal service communication review
manual.V13: documented configuration review supplied by the operators
manual.V14: data classification review and inspection of retention and logging configuration
manual.V15: architecture, dependency inventory and supply-chain review of the codebase
manual.V16: log pipeline and error handling review with access to the logging systems
manual.V17: WebRTC implementation review, only when the target actually carries real-time media
